headline: TROILUS DRILLS 8.84 g/t AuEq OVER 4.8M AT Z87 — HIGH-GRADE CONFIRMED 400M BEYOND QUEBEC PIT SHELL
snippet: Troilus Mining Corp. announced today that drill hole TLG-ZJ20-222-EXT26 returned 8.84 g/t gold-equivalent (7.02 g/t Au, 21.63 g/t Ag, 1.03% Cu) over 4.8 metres — including 23.58 g/t AuEq over 1 metre — at the Z87 deposit in north-central Quebec, extending the known high-grade zone up to 400 metres beyond the current resource pit shell and 300 metres beyond the mineral resource model boundary. Five holes totalling 2,915 metres targeted down-plunge continuity of the J Zone and all intersected mineralization, demonstrating the Z87 high-grade core remains open at depth and that pit optimization models will need to be revised upward.

headline: ISOENERGY + DISA URANIUM CLOSES — $105M RAISED WITH BHP VENTURES, TEMBO CAPITAL; IsoEnergy RETAINS 33%
snippet: IsoEnergy Ltd. (TSX: ISO) and DISA Technologies closed their deal on August 19, forming DISA Uranium Corporation with a concurrent US$105 million private placement backed by BHP Ventures, Tembo Capital, Galvanize Climate Solutions, Valor Equity Partners, Evok Innovations, Halliburton Labs, and Veriten. IsoEnergy contributed five permitted, past-producing conventional uranium mines in Utah — Tony M, Daneros, Rim, Sage Plain, and Flatiron — in exchange for approximately 33% of DISA Uranium on a fully diluted basis. The combined entity pairs IsoEnergy's production-ready Utah portfolio with DISA's proprietary HPSA uranium recovery technology, creating a U.S.-domestic uranium platform with strategic backing from mining (BHP), energy (Halliburton), and climate finance simultaneously.

headline: COPPER SUPPLY CRUNCH BREAKS: LME STOCKS SURGE 50%+ IN THREE DAYS, SPOT PRICE DROPS TO $6.50/lb
snippet: London Metal Exchange on-warrant copper inventories surged more than 50% over three trading days — rising 63,000 tonnes with gains across Asia, the U.S., and Europe — sharply easing the supply squeeze the LME had responded to with emergency measures on August 14. The closely-watched spot-vs-three-month spread collapsed from a $545-per-tonne backwardation Monday to $207 by Wednesday, and spot copper dropped to $6.50 per pound (650 cents/lb), down 3.47% on the session. Copper had fallen 47% in LME inventories from late May to mid-August; the sudden reversal raises the question of whether the record rally reflected durable tightness or a short-term arbitrage trade ahead of potential U.S. tariffs.

headline: CRITICAL ONE (CRTL) HITS GOLD + 36.9% ANTIMONY AT HOWELLS LAKE — DUAL CRITICAL MINERAL FIND IN ONTARIO
snippet: Critical One Energy (CSE: CRTL; OTCQB: MMTLF) announced August 20 that hole HWL-2026-016 at its Howells Lake Antimony-Gold Project in northwestern Ontario returned 31.5 metres grading 4.9% antimony — including 1 metre at 36.9% Sb and 4 metres at 21.2% Sb — and separately intercepted 17.0 metres at 1.3 g/t gold. Companion hole HWL-2026-011 returned 12.0 metres at 1.3 g/t gold including 1 metre at 9.1 g/t Au. The results extend Howells Lake's antimony footprint 70 metres northeast of previously drilled holes, ~120 km west of the Ring of Fire access corridor. Antimony — used in flame retardants, semiconductors, and military ammunition — has no producing domestic source in North America.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER (SCMI) MINTO PHASE 2: 13.12% CuEq OVER 1.9M AS PROGRAM CROSSES 97,000 METRES DRILLED
snippet: Selkirk Copper Ltd. (TSXV: SCMI) released additional Phase 2 drill results from the Minto Project in Yukon today, reporting infill hole 26SCM190 at Minto North returned 6.01% Cu, 8.77 g/t Au, and 36.6 g/t Ag (13.12% copper-equivalent) over 1.93 metres within a broader 33.2-metre interval at 1.49% CuEq. Step-out 26SCM205 returned 3.87% CuEq over 3.7 metres. The company has now completed over 97,000 metres of drilling in eleven months; the 50,000-metre Phase 2 program is 75% complete, with a PEA targeted for Q3 2026, and the July resource update established 940 million pounds of M&I copper — a 182% increase over 2025.

headline: TRANS CANADA GOLD (TTG) COMPLETES PHASE 1 UNDERGROUND DRILL AND PASSES BC MINISTRY OF MINES INSPECTION
snippet: Trans Canada Gold Corp. (CVE: TTG) announced August 20 it has successfully completed Phase 1 underground diamond drilling on Bear Mountain at the Harrison Lake Gold Project in southwestern British Columbia and passed a mine inspection by the BC Ministry of Mines — a permitting milestone that clears the site for continued underground operations. Core will be analyzed by PhotonAssay, now the standard method for high-grade nuggety gold; assay results are pending. The program targeted multiple gold zones based on successful historical drill programs showing high-grade extensions at shallow depth.

headline: "WARSH SAYS AS LITTLE AS POSSIBLE" — JACKSON HOLE HYPE MAY OUTRUN THE FED CHAIR'S OWN PLAYBOOK
snippet: An InvestingLive analysis argues that market expectations for a major policy signal from Fed Chair Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole keynote fundamentally misread his track record: since taking office May 22, Warsh has shortened every post-meeting statement, given deliberately evasive press conference answers, and framed his approach as explicitly independent of market pricing. A speech billed around 'big picture questions' — not near-term guidance — is consistent with that pattern. For junior mining investors, this is the flip side of the Jackson Hole gold bull case: the most likely outcome is Warsh says very little, markets reprice, and the gold bid softens briefly before the underlying structural drivers reassert.

headline: GOLD PAUSES AT $4,490 AFTER 4% SURGE — CENTRAL BANKS BOUGHT RECORD 288.9 TONNES IN Q2, MOST IN HISTORY
snippet: Gold consolidated around $4,490 on August 20 after Wednesday's 4.13% surge to $4,512, as traders paused to assess the extent of the rally while September rate-hike odds remained suppressed at 33%. The structural bid beneath the market is deepening: central banks globally purchased a net 288.9 tonnes of gold in Q2 2026 — a 62% increase from the 177.9 tonnes bought in Q2 2025 and the strongest second-quarter total in World Gold Council records — with Goldman Sachs projecting approximately 60 tonnes of monthly central bank purchases through year-end as reserve managers diversify away from U.S. dollar assets.

headline: LITHIUM SINKS TO 5-MONTH LOW AT CNY 140,000 — BALD HILL, FINNISS, CATL JIANXIAWO RESTARTS OVERWHELM DEMAND
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices fell to CNY 140,000 per tonne in August — a five-month low — as supply returned faster than expected from three major restarts: Mineral Resources' Bald Hill (WA, after 18 months on care and maintenance), Core Lithium's Finniss project, and CATL's Jianxiawo mine, one of the world's largest, which cleared security permits. Despite lithium demand in stationary energy storage growing approximately 71% in 2025 with 55% more projected in 2026, the concurrent supply reactivations have overwhelmed the recovery. For TSX-V and ASX lithium explorers, spot prices remain above 2024-2025 lows but the restart wave underscores how quickly the market tips from deficit to glut when producer incentives align.
